newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Aug 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Refined oil prices expected to rise by 4.1 percent on the domestic market in September.
- Four women in the reshuffled cabinet for the first time since the independence of Morocco in 1956.
- Cement firm Ciments du Maroc expected to show positive results of up to $6.6 million in 1997.
- Largest conglomerate Societe Narionale d'Investissement to improve its sales by five percent by end 1997.
- Somafic firm, a subsidiary of BMCI bank issued $14.4 million notes on the Casablanca stock exchange to reduce its debt.
- Societe Epargne Croissance firm was delisted from the Casablanca bourse after it failed to comply with the market's reform rules.
- Leading Wafabank opens a branch in southern Spanish city of Algesiras.

- Morocco to start technical studies on natural gas nationwide use. Story refers to the possibility of use by local industry and households of up to 1.5 billion cubic metres of Algerian gas in future.
